correctness.rationale: In the linear word P^k# with q,k>=2, distinct letters, and r_i>=2, a factor containing # occurs only once. Every other nonunary factor has a unique phase modulo |P|, since its first ordered letter change fixes that phase. It is right-maximal exactly when it is a suffix of P^(k-1): it then occurs both before the final # and at the previous period boundary before a_0. A unary factor shorter than its run has the self follower and its cyclic successor, and if it belongs to the last run it can also have #. The full unary last run has the two boundary followers a_0 and #, whereas the other full unary runs have only one. These cases, including the empty word, place every extension under a listed candidate in suffix order. The candidates are all extensions and have distinct last two symbols (the two long ones end in a_(q-1)a_0 and a_(q-1)#), so none is a suffix of another. This also supplies the suffix direction intended in the aside about a_0 in proof step 2. Each short candidate has one end offset per period, distinct between the first and last positions of any run by r_i>=2. The long candidates have just the last-period first position and the terminal position as their respective single endings. Every smallest set chooses one from each disjoint end class, giving 2q+1 positions and k^(2q-1) sets. For attractors, the q+1 one-letter factors give the lower bound. Choose each last run position of the first period and #. A nonunary factor without # can be shifted so that its first ordered change aligns with the first-period occurrence of that change: the leading unary segment fits in the chosen first-period run, so the shifted occurrence stays inside the text and meets the selected run end. Unary factors end-align there, and marked factors meet #. The supplied literal-substring verifier and captured output were inspected, not run: 246 parameter instances, 12358 extensions and four direct counts of minimum sets corroborate the proof; these are not infinite certificates.

value.rationale: Distinct contiguous letter runs isolate local within-run branching from periodic phase and sentinel branching, making this a natural family in which to understand exact suffixient complexity. The theorem does more than compute the size: it exhibits every optimum, explains why varying run lengths does not affect their number, and distinguishes this suffix-ending condition from the attractor invariant on the same text.
